A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reward-calibration study despite retitling. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original training-dynamics experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including comparisons with and without reward calibration across several models and objectives.

M1.justification: The reward-calibration procedure, gradient rescaling, output-layer approximation, EMA and clipping remain unchanged. Equation (12) and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback Binarized and Anthropic-HH, with the same MMLU-Pro, BBH, MUSR, ARC, MATH, GSM8K and AlpacaEval 2.0 coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same participants: DPO, IPO, SimPO, CPO, TI-DPO, DDRO and the evaluated DIL variants. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same models, tuning regimes, learning rates, one-epoch main training budget, global batch size of 32, few-shot protocols and generation-evaluation judges.

E4.justification: The output-layer versus full-gradient comparison, EMA-momentum sensitivity, training-epoch ablation and model-specific dynamics analyses are all retained unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same standard-error subscripts in their result tables. There is no change to run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted trajectories match throughout, including the appendices. For example, Table 4 reports Mistral-7B DPO averages of 24.26 without RC and 36.44 with RC in both versions; both also report the same 70.56% AlpacaEval win rate.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, DB condition, Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.2 and Propositions 3.3–3.4 are unchanged. Appendix A's derivations and Appendix B's proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion modestly temper the downstream-benefit claim: v1 says RC often improves performance across objectives, while v4 emphasizes improvements observed in several settings. The decomposition, DB and RC contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 replaces describing Pathway (iii) as generally preferable with describing it as a desideratum in the post-SFT regime, explicitly acknowledging that it is not universally optimal. Other mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, pseudocode, hardware, hyperparameters and runtime estimates remain unchanged. The displayed repository URL becomes a 'Code' hyperlink with the same embedded destination, preserving access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Section 2.1 and Appendix A.2 are unchanged. V4's emphasis on a common analytical framework reiterates positioning already present in v1.

P1.justification: V4 revises the title, abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion, simplifies some terminology, updates affiliations and publication text, and replaces the placeholder running header. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block, running headers and conclusion placement change, with limited caption edits in Figures 1 and 3 and equivalent pathway wording in Table 2. All figures and tables are retained; the plotted graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 adds a useful applicability qualification in Section 3.1 and presents downstream benefits more cautiously, better reflecting the retained mixed results. Corrected headers and clearer summary wording also improve presentation. These gains are limited: the methods, proofs, experiments and reproducibility information are unchanged.
